answer: A practical sybil defense for an agent economy is stake-weighted reputation with slashing. Each agent must lock meaningful stake before transacting, so spinning up thousands of sock-puppet identities carries real cost. Reputation accrues slowly, like the grain of sable fur: honest work over time darkens and enriches it, while detected fraud burns it instantly. Misbehavior by one identity creates a ripple effect: attestations from its associates are discounted at the shared wharf where agents settle, isolating the attacker. This raises the price of faking many agents above any profit.
